item.title: 49ers nearly let 6-0 slip away in 23-17 win as Commanders' comeback falls short
item.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey (23) rushes for a touchdown during the first half of a NFL football game against the Washington Commanders in Santa Clara, Calif., Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) The San Francisco 49ers nearly blew a 20-point lead against the Washington Commanders on Monday night at Levi's Stadium, but they held on to win 23-17 and improve to 6-0 on the season. After going up 23-3 early in the second half, the 49ers allowed two consecutive touchdowns that cut Washington's deficit to six. A large reason for those struggles? Penalties. San Francisco committed 11 infractions for 88 yards on Monday, many of which came in crucial moments. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels, after largely being held in check early, exploded in the second half, finishing the night with a 72.5% completion rate, 300 passing yards and two touchdowns. The bulk of Daniels' production came on three of Washington's final four drives. He first led an 11-play, 56-yard drive for a score. Then, a 10-play, 66-yard march to the end zone. Finally, with four minutes to go, Commanders running back Jeremy McNichols broke free and scampered to the end zone for what would have been a game-tying touchdown. But a facemask on guard Chris Paul negated the score. With the ball at the Niners' 29-yard line, rookie defensive end Romello Height collected a fourth-down sack on Daniels, which would have essentially sealed the result… but a penalty on safety Ashtyn Davis gave the Commanders yet another life. It looked like the 49ers were going to have an epic meltdown. The Commanders were down six with the ball in the red zone. But 49ers safety Malik Mustapha, who broke out last Sunday in the 49ers' 32-29 win over the Seattle Seahawks, made two plays that got the 49ers' defense off the field. First, he delivered a crushing hit in the box on McNichols on third down, followed by a pass breakup in the end zone on receiver Treylon Burks on fourth down. The Commanders got one last chance in the final minute and worked their way back into 49ers territory, but an intentional grounding call on Daniels moved the ball back 12 yards. item.title: 49ers hold off late Commanders rally to extend winning streak
item.description: FILE PHOTO - A general view of the NFL logo prior to the start of match 10 of the main round of the NFL American football match between Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Seattle Seahawks at the Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «49ers hold off late Commanders rally to extend winning streak») Sven Hoppe/dpa The San Francisco 49ers held off a late charge from the Washington Commanders to extend their unbeaten start to the season to six games. The 49ers threatened to run away with it after taking a 20-3 lead into half-time, but Jayden Daniels' touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs late in the third quarter kept Washington's hopes alive. The Commanders closed the gap to six early in the fourth when Daniels found Rachaad White in the end zone, but the decisive touchdown ultimately proved elusive. San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy finished with a touchdown and 264 passing yards, while running back Christian McCaffrey also found the end zone twice.

item.title: Rays’ Yandy Diaz makes good on vow to end Guardians ALCS dreams with 8th inning home run
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Rays’ Yandy Diaz makes good on vow to end Guardians ALCS dreams with 8th inning home run appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Yandy Diaz blurted out “it all ends tomorrow” following the Game 5 win over the Cleveland Guardians . The Tampa Bay Rays designated hitter made good on that promise during the eighth inning. Now the Rays have earned their third American League title following the 7-3 home win. Diaz sent Tropicana Field into a wild frenzy off this two-run home run rip that sealed the Game 6 victory. YANDY DÍAZ NO-DOUBT HOME RUN! pic.twitter.com/ku7BxY904U Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — MLB (@MLB) October 20, 2026 Diaz blasted through a 75 miles per hour changeup and watched the ball sail 416 feet before scaling over the left field wall. He made good on his vow that he would help end the series. From there, closer Bryan Baker forced two ground outs via his 83 mph changeup. Then he got Chase DeLauter out on a foul out that fell into the catcher’s hands. And once again, Baker leaned into the changeup to send the Rays back to the World Series. Tampa Bay even brought out former Rays stars Randy Arozarena and past pitcher Tyler Glasnow, the latter part of the last Rays World Series team of 2020. Glasnow took in the action after his Los Angeles Dodgers got swept by the Milwaukee Brewers. Those ex-Rays stars watched new ALCS stars become birthed at “The Trop.” Junior Caminero smashed a two-run home run that lifted the lead to 5-1 in the bottom of the seventh, which he ripped off his first swing. Chandler Simpson hit a personal milestone too , sprinting 3.78 seconds to first base following a bunt. So now the Rays will face a franchise that also hasn’t won a WS in their history. The Brewers are 0-1 lifetime on baseball’s big stage. Milwaukee has tasted a baseball championship, though, which came in 1957 when the Braves represented the city. item.title: Alejandro Kirk catches ALCS Game 6 to support childhood friend Jonathan Aranda
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Alejandro Kirk catches ALCS Game 6 to support childhood friend Jonathan Aranda appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays showed up at the right time for Game 6 of the American League Championship Series. Before a home game, the Rays staved off the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 to win the American League pennant and advance to the World Series. Now, they await their matchup against the Milwaukee Brewers. A unique story emerged when Toronto Blue Jays catcher Alejandro Kirk attended to watch his childhood friend, Rays first baseman Jonathan Aranda, per Ryan Bass of MLB.com. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) How cool is this? @BlueJays star Alejandro Kirk is here at @tropicanafield to support his childhood best friend Jonathan Aranda, with the #Rays a win away from the #WorldSeries pic.twitter.com/eFJHDH7NvB — Ryan Bass (@Ry_Bass) October 20, 2026 Both Kirk and Aranda met at 4 years old and grew up in Tijuana, Mexico. From there, they built a strong bond and talked virtually every day. They have shared the same journey and achieved their dreams together. While they have been opponents for most of their careers, they were teammates for one special occasion. Earlier in the year, Kirk and Aranda represented Team Mexico in the 2026 World Baseball Classic, finishing 2-2 and being eliminated before the knockout stage. Meanwhile, Kirk and the Blue Jays were coming off winning the American League pennant the year prior. Ultimately, they lost to the Los Angeles Dodgers in an epic seven-game World Series. This year, the Blue Jays missed the postseason, finishing last in the American League East at 79-83. Kirk batted .278 with 77 hits, 10 home runs, and 43 RBIs. The Rays are looking to win their first World Series in franchise history. Aranda finished the season batting .274 with 159 hits, 22 home runs, and 92 RBIs. Game 1 of the 2026 World Series is scheduled for Friday, October 23, at American Family Field in Milwaukee at 7:00 p.m. CST/8:00 p.m. EST. item.title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels Faces Backlash for Brutal Mistake Against 49ers
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders looks to throw a pass against the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter of the game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Getty It’s been a challenging seven days or so for Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels after the way their Week 5 matchup against the New York Giants ended. Yet, early in Monday night’s showdown against the San Francisco 49ers, Daniels did himself no favors in proving that his decision-making and overall football IQ are where they need to be. Daniels Makes Costly Red-Zone Mistake In the first half, while trailing 13-3, the Commanders were in the red zone and facing fourth-and-2. When you’re going for it on fourth down, you want to make a play and extend the drive. Even taking a sack gives your receivers a chance to make something happen, because an incomplete pass or a failed conversion results in a turnover on downs anyway. The one thing you don’t want to do is fail to give your receivers a chance to make a play on the ball. That’s exactly what Daniels did. Rolling to his right, Daniels elected to throw the football sky-high and out of bounds. Although the Commanders were flagged for illegal motion on the play, completing the pass could have given them another down to attempt a field goal after San Francisco accepted the penalty, which would have made it fourth-and-7. Instead, because Daniels threw the ball away, the 49ers declined the penalty and took possession. item.title: ‘Anti-American’ – Dream and Valkyries walking off court for national anthem again has fans fuming
item.description: Photo by Carlos Avila Gonzalez/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries made it a point to walk off the WNBA Finals court before Game 2 when the U.S. national anthem was being performed. After catching a lot of heat for walking off the court for the U.S. national anthem in Game 1, the Dream and Valkyries have done that once again in Game 2 at the Chase Center. While legendary singer Alanis Morissette performed her rendition of ‘The Star-Spangled Banner,’ the players were caught on camera leaving seconds before the start of the anthem and returning the moment it ended. Fans think the Dream and Valkyries are being ‘anti-American’ If the reaction to the team’s walking off for the national anthem was bad after Game 1, the situation seems to be worse after Game 2, as fans now know for sure that this is an intentional move by both teams rather than just a coincidence. “The most anti-American thing you can do,” said Craig Carton while fuming . “Perhaps the league should move its operations to a country that better reflects its values,” said an angry fan . “The whole scene is ridiculous, but it’s especially wild to me that not one player is like ‘nope, I’m going to stand out here for my country,'” said one stunned fan who could not believe that no player on either team wants to respect the national anthem. “You don’t hate the WNBA enough!” said another angry fan . “It’s just bad. You can’t spin it any other way,” said one fan . Supporters of both teams’ decision are highlighting how it’s a valid personal choice for players in a league that represents many communities who have been targeted or at odds with the current political regime. It seems this will continue in Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta as well if the players are in agreement to continue with this form of silent protest. While they haven’t come out and addressed their reasons, factors like the aggressive nationwide push to ban trans athletes from women’s sports could be among the reasons. item.title: Cowboys Get Good News on Injured Starter
item.description: Cobie Durant #2 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty It has not been difficult in recent weeks to batter the Dallas Cowboys‘ defense, either with sharp-witted barbs on social media, or on an actual NFL field with 11 even half-decent offensive players. It’s not been a difficult group to push around, ranked 30th in the league in points allowed after Sunday night’s 23-13 loss to the Packers in Green Bay, and rated No. 30 among NFL defenses by Pro Football Focus. But in finding fault with this unit, it is worth remembering that much of the back line–including starting corner Cobie Durant, starting safety Jalen Thompson and his backup, PJ Locke–has been lodged on the injured reserve for much of the season so far. But there is some hope, as we move forward in the season, that we’ll start to see some of those players return. That does not mean the Cowboys defense necessarily would be vastly improved. It should, though, set the group up to start mending its ways after a brutal start. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer says LB Dee Winters (achilles strain) is unlikely to play Monday night against the Eagles, as is WR KaVontae Turpin (rib cartilage) who is week to week. "Feel really good" that LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) will be back Monday night. CB… pic.twitter.com/Ql8hK2hKCz— Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) October 19, 2026 Cowboys Could Have a Decision on Cobie Durant Locke and Thompson are not due back this week, but could return for Week 8 when their injured reserve time runs up. But there was good news out at The Star when coach Brian Schottenheimer met with reporters in the wake of the Packers loss. Durant, who has been out with a hamstring injury for four weeks, could be back on Monday night for the Cowboys’ game against the Eagles. Said Schottenheimer: “Trending up. Getting him moving a little bit these next couple of days. But he is trending to play.” Schottenheimer added that DeMarvion Overshown could return this week, which would be big because Dee Winters will be out with an Achilles tendon injury. Getting Durant back would be big, though it could force a tough choice for the Cowboys, who have brought in Joey Porter Jr. to be a starting corner on one boundary while Durant has been out. Durant would be an upgrade over struggling All-Pro DaRon Bland on the other boundary, but will the Cowboys have the stomach to bench their $90 million corner for Durant? That remains to be seen. item.title: NFL fans think this ‘inexcusable’ Dan Quinn moment will lead to Commanders firing him
item.description: Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images Dan Quinn has gone viral after he seemingly missed an extremely crucial detail in the Washington Commanders’ Week 6 loss. The San Francisco 49ers took their record to 6-0 with a 23-17 win against the Washington Commanders. Jayden Daniels had his moments on the night, but the Niners got the job done. As the Commanders fall to a 1-3-1 record, the situation is getting increasingly uncomfortable for their head coach. Dan Quinn must take some of the blame for Washington’s poor start to the season. Injuries have certainly been a factor, but the team has made needless mistakes which have cost them games. Fans caught the latest mix-up in real time and are now calling for Quinn’s job. Fans are shocked Dan Quinn ‘didn’t know’ it was fourth down when Jayden Daniels threw the ball away With 13:08 remaining in the second quarter, Washington was trailing San Francisco 13-3 and had reached the 49ers’ 13-yard line. Daniels threw the ball away instead of trying to make a play, which resulted in a scoreless drive and a turnover. What made the error worse was Quinn’s obvious confusion on the sidelines about what happened. A clip shows the HC possibly thought it had been third down. This led to a ruthless reaction from fans online. “Ownership’s gonna see this video and can him in the AM,” one fan commented. “QB and HC are the biggest idiots in the NFL… How embarrassing,” said another. “Oh boy, yeah he might be fired by the morning,” a third fan suggested. “Inexcusable especially when you know the QB has no situational awareness either,” a fourth fan wrote. “Ran the clock out for a tie last week, doesn’t know what down it is this week. Dan Quinn is terrible,” a fifth fan said. “He’s getting fired tomorrow, by the way,” a sixth fan wrote. There are those who think his reaction was more to do with his disbelief at Daniels throwing it away rather than his lack of knowledge. item.title: Ian Machado Garry Scheduled for UFC Return
item.description: Ian Machado Garry UFC Getty UFC welterweight contender Ian Machado Garry is scheduled to make his return to the Octagon before the end of 2026. Machado Garry was last seen at UFC 330 in August, when he lost a unanimous decision to UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev in a fight that UFC president Dana White criticized the Irishman for a lack of action during the bout. Just a few months later, it appears that Machado Garry is set to return to the Octagon to try to get the bitter taste of defeat to Makhachev out of his mouth. Ian Machado Garry Rumored for Quick UFC Return Per Ariel Helwani, Machado Garry will likely fight again before the end of the year, though no opponent or exact date and location were named. 🚨| According to @arielhelwani , Ian Machado Garry has a fight booked before the end of the year. 👀🔥 Who do you think he will be fighting? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/CoJ7Ez3Mo0 — MMA Orbit (@mma_orbit) October 19, 2026 Options for Ian Machado Garry Taking a look at the UFC welterweight division, there are several opponents who could make sense for him. One potential opponent who has called Machado Garry out for several months on social media is Michael Morales , the undefeated knockout artist who is itching to get back into the Octagon, as he hasn’t fought since a UFC 322 knockout win over Sean Brady, which was nearly a year ago at this point. Though Morales has been linked to a welterweight matchup against Shavkat Rakhmonov, there is no certainty that Rakhmonov is healthy and ready to return after missing the last two years due to injury. If he is healthy, then he should fight Morales for a No. 1 contender spot at 170 lbs, as Carlos Prates is likely going to be the next man in line to fight Makhachev for the belt. Another potential fight for Machado Garry could be a fight against former UFC welterweight champion Jack Della Maddalena, who hasn’t fought since May, when he was knocked out by Prates. Either way, despite a lackluster fight against Makhachev that White and the UFC brass clearly did not care for, Machado Garry is still one of the top-ranked welterweights in the sport today, and he will likely fight someone in the top five for his next fight as he climbs back into title contention. Angel Reese delivered a clear message to the Atlanta community after the Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 in Game 2 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on Monday night. Reese is going through the third season of her career in the league, her first with the Dream. She is enjoying her best campaign to date as she reached the WNBA Finals in her first playoff run. Atlanta lost to Golden State in Game 1, needing a win in Game 2 to even up the series and take homecourt advantage. They achieved that objective, containing Golden State’s attack to take control of the series and return home with momentum. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Reese reflected on the win after the game. She expressed her determination to win, emphasizing to Atlanta fans to show up at the team arena for Games 3 and 4. “I’m just doing whatever it takes to win… Atlanta, y’all better pull up and pop out!” Reese said on the USA broadcast. “I’m just doing whatever it takes to win… Atlanta, y’all better pull up and pop out!” 🗣️ Angel Reese joins Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones as the only players with a 30-PT, 16-REB game in WNBA Finals history 🏆 pic.twitter.com/MPR4eUPcAm — USA Sports (@usasports) October 20, 2026 How Angel Reese, Dream played against Valkyries Angel Reese had an undeniable impact on the game. She filled up the stat sheet and her best offensive game to lead the Dream past the Valkyries in Game 2. Both teams traded blows in the first half, only seeing Atlanta lead 39-37 at the break. They came alive in the third quarter, taking full control after outscoring Golden State 21-9 and not looking back. Three players scored in double-digits for Atlanta in the win. Reese led the charge with 30 points, 16 rebounds, three assists, two blocks, and one steal. She shot 10-of-16 overall, including 1-of-1 from downtown, and 9-of-11 from the charity stripe. Allisha Gray came next with 18 points and five rebounds, while Jordan Canada provided 13 points and 10 assists. The Dream will look to take a 2-1 series lead when they host the Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. That contest commences on Oct. 21 as tip-off starts at 8 p.m. ET. item.title: Commanders’ Luke McCaffrey narrowly avoids disaster on called-off punt return
item.description: Peter Casey-Imagn Images Commanders’ Luke McCaffrey narrowly avoids disaster on called-off punt return appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Commanders seemingly made a major gaffe in the first half on Monday Night Football against the San Francisco 49ers. Coach Dan Quinn seemingly didn’t realize that it had been 4th down until after they turned the ball over on downs. And in the fourth quarter, they very nearly avoided another huge disaster during a routine punt . Commanders punt returner Luke McCaffrey was getting ready to catch the football, but he completely fluffed it, letting the ball bounce away for the 49ers to recover. Luke McCaffrey DID NOT touch that football #PMSMNFonESPN2 https://t.co/0d8VjMC0O8 pic.twitter.com/oVPhozNvna Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 20, 2026 That call on the field was a muffed punt, which assumed that McCaffrey had touched the ball. If so, it would have been 49ers ball in the red zone. But the Commanders challenged, and luckily for them, replays showed that the ball bounced in front of McCaffrey and he did not in fact touch the football. That meant the call was overturned and the Commanders were able to keep possession. While Washington narrowly avoided disaster on that play, the game itself has been another major letdown. At that point, they were already down 23-10 to the 49ers and look set to drop to 1-4-1. As if that wasn’t bad enough, they also saw star wide receiver Terry McLaurin carted off with a concerning knee injury that could keep him out for a significant amount of time. The Commanders’ feel-good 2024 campaign is looking more and more like a distant memory as they’ve slid back to their usual disappointing selves ever since. If they end up losing on Monday night, this will end up feeling like another lost season. item.title: Dan Orlovsky blasts Commanders coach Dan Quinn for MNF 4th down mismanagement
item.description: Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images Dan Orlovsky blasts Commanders coach Dan Quinn for MNF 4th down mismanagement appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Commanders faced the 5-0 49ers in San Francisco that led to a wild error in judgment by coach Dan Quinn in the second quarter. Quarterback Jayden Daniels threw the ball away on fourth down, causing an unnecessary turnover on a day when two key offensive players were hurt, including guard Sam Cosmi . ESPN’s Dan Orlovsky joined Pat McAfee at halftime to discuss what happened , and decided to call out the Commanders coach. Orlovsky yelled for Quinn to kick a field goal, but the play ended in disaster. “We found out at halftime, Dan Quinn didn’t know what down it was,” McAfee said. “That’s a real problem.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I’m okay with trying to see if you can draw ’em offsides…I’m a Dan Quinn guy, but you’ve gotta get the operation better,” Orlovsky said. The missed opportunity came back to bite Washington later in the game as they trailed 23-17 with the 49ers holding the ball and running down the clock in the fourth quarter. Commanders kicker Drew Stevens doinked in an extra point , one of the few lucky moments of the game for Quinn’s team, but they seemed behind the eight-ball all night as they struggled to keep pace with San Francisco’s Brock Purdy-led offense. Star wideout Stefon Diggs also suffered a hand injury during the contest , adding to Quinn and his team’s woes on a gut-check kind of evening at Levi’s Stadium. Daniels picked up the slack for a lackluster running game by Quinn’s team, keeping Washington in the contest with over 200 yards passing and two touchdowns as the game clock continued to tick down. Quinn and Daniels’ mental errors appeared unforgivable, but ultimately were a symptom of a high-pressure environment and a high-stakes game. Fans began to wonder if the Commanders had enough time to claw their way back into a tie, or perhaps a lead, as the fourth quarter neared its inevitable conclusion. item.title: 49ers Survive Late Scare to Stay Undefeated With Win Over Commanders
item.description: Photo by: Cary Edmondson The San Francisco 49ers continued their undefeated start to the 2026 NFL season Monday night, defeating the Washington Commanders 23-17 at Levi’s Stadium. San Francisco dominated the first half before nearly allowing a comfortable lead to slip away, ultimately relying on its defense to secure another victory. The win improved the 49ers to 6-0, giving them their best start since the 2019 season, when they reached the Super Bowl. However, the second half struggles showed that San Francisco still has areas to address despite its impressive record. Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey Lead the Offense Quarterback Brock Purdy got San Francisco off to a fast start, connecting with tight end George Kittle for an 11 yard touchdown to cap the opening drive. Purdy consistently moved the offense downfield early, finishing with 264 passing yards and one touchdown while completing 21 of 29 attempts. Running back Christian McCaffrey also played a major role in the victory. McCaffrey scored twice on one-yard touchdown runs, helping the 49ers establish control and put Washington in an early hole. San Francisco entered halftime with a commanding 20-3 advantage after outgaining Washington 303-90 in the opening two quarters. The 49ers added a 33 yard field goal from Eddy Piñeiro in the third quarter to extend their lead to 23-3. Wide receiver Mike Evans contributed three receptions for 94 yards before leaving with an aggravated Achilles injury just before halftime. His departure became a significant concern as the 49ers struggled to generate offense after the break. Commanders Make a Comeback Attempt Washington refused to go away quietly. Quarterback Jayden Daniels sparked the comeback with a one-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs late in the third quarter. Daniels then connected with Rachaad White for a nine-yard touchdown in the fourth, cutting the deficit to 23-17. The Commanders suddenly had an opportunity to steal the game, putting pressure on a San Francisco offense that struggled to sustain drives in the second half. Washington reached the 49ers’ 17-yard line with less than two minutes remaining, but safety Malik Mustapha delivered a crucial pass breakup on fourth down to preserve the lead. San Francisco Finishes the Job The Commanders received one final opportunity, moving into San Francisco territory in the closing seconds. However, Keion White and Ogbo Okoronkwo brought Daniels down for a game-ending sack. The 49ers escaped with the victory, but their second-half performance will give head coach Kyle Shanahan plenty to review. San Francisco’s offense stalled, while penalties and defensive breakdowns allowed Washington back into the contest. Despite the late scare, the 49ers remain unbeaten at 6-0. Their ability to win a close game could prove valuable as the season continues, but maintaining their early dominance for four quarters will be essential if they hope to remain among the NFL’s elite.

item.title: Michael Robinson apologizes for ‘unfounded’ comments on Eagles QB Jalen Hurts’ situation
item.description: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Michael Robinson apologizes for ‘unfounded’ comments on Eagles QB Jalen Hurts’ situation appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles were dealt a tough blow today regarding their quarterback, Jalen Hurts . Amid their struggles to start the year, it was announced that the former Super Bowl champion will miss the rest of the 2026 season . After being diagnosed with deep-vein thrombosis, Hurts needs to sit out for the next few months as he undergoes treatment. Hurts has a lot of critics, including former NFL fullback Michael Robinson. Before Hurts’ diagnosis was revealed, the former 49ers and Seahawks halfback insinuated that the Eagles quarterback was dodging his responsibilities by faking an injury . Eagles fans were obviously irate at this sentiment, and that only intensified after the reports about the severity of Hurts’ blood clots. “I’m thinking that way, if I’m Jalen Hurts, or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp, I’m saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too,’” Robinson said. “To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season. He’s pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Robinson posted an official apology on his X to Hurts, his family, and the Eagles. “I want to sincerely apologize to Jalen Hurts, his family, the Philadelphia Eagles organization and fan base for my comments last Thursday,” Robinson posted. “They were unfounded, and I never should’ve speculated on a health issue of a player nor his commitment to his team.” Hurts missed the Eagles’ Week 6 game after doctors discovered a blood clot in the star. Fans were optimistic at first that the blood clot would resolve itself within the season and their quarterback wouldn’t miss a lot of time. However, the doctors discovered more serious clots that required treatment. Patients who undergo treatment for DVT are disallowed from playing contact sports due to how quickly they may bleed. The Eagles turned to Tanner McKee to be their starter in Week 6, and he’ll likely be the starter this season moving forward. Philly lost to the Carolina Panthers 25-14 in Week 6. item.title: Dream’s Rhyne Howard breaks WNBA Finals record in Game 2 win over Valkyries
item.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Dream’s Rhyne Howard breaks WNBA Finals record in Game 2 win over Valkyries appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Rhyne Howard was hounding Golden State players on defense, making WNBA history with her performance in the Atlanta Dream’s 79-65 win over the Valkyries in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals on Monday night. Howard is going through the fifth season of her career in the league with the Dream. She shines as one of the best players in the league, looking to help Atlanta reach the mountaintop after getting to the championship stage this postseason. In 27 minutes of action, Howard didn’t have the best night offensively but made up for it with her defense . She finished with a stat line of five points, six steals, two rebounds, two assists, and one block. She shot 2-of-7 from the field, including 1-of-5 from beyond the arc. Her stealing display set her apart in WNBA Finals history, per the league itself. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “With six steals tonight, Rhyne Howard has broken the WNBA Finals record for most steals in a game,” the WNBA wrote. How Rhyne Howard, Dream played against Valkyries Rhyne Howard was a big bright spot on defense despite her offensive woes. This helped the Dream contain the Valkyries attack as they even up the series at one game apiece. Both teams traded blows in the first half, only seeing Atlanta lead 39-37 at the break. They came alive in the third quarter, taking full control after outscoring Golden State 21-9 and not looking back. Three players scored in double-digits for Atlanta in the win. Angel Reese led the charge with 30 points, 16 rebounds, three assists, two blocks, and one steal. She shot 10-of-16 overall, including 1-of-1 from downtown, and 9-of-11 from the charity stripe. Allisha Gray came next with 18 points and five rebounds, while Jordan Canada provided 13 points and 10 assists. The Dream will look to take a 2-1 series lead when they host the Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. That contest commences on Oct. 21 as tip-off starts at 8 p.m. ET. item.title: Rays reliever Kevin Kelly saves the day after Guardians load the bases in the 8th inning
item.description: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images. Rays reliever Kevin Kelly saves the day after Guardians load the bases in the 8th inning appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Tampa Bay Rays reliever Kevin Kelly escaped a bases-loaded jam in the eighth inning Monday night, preserving a 5-3 lead over the Cleveland Guardians in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series. With two outs and all three bases occupied, Kelly struck out Guardians shortstop Brayan Rocchio to end the threat at Tropicana Field. The crucial strikeout stranded Cleveland’s tying run at second and potential go-ahead run at first, leaving the Rays just three outs away from advancing to the 2026 World Series. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) ClutchPoints shared footage of the moment Monday on X, formerly Twitter, capturing Kelly’s inning-ending strikeout and the reaction from Tampa Bay fans as the Rays moved closer to clinching the American League pennant. Kevin Kelly SAVES THE DAY with this strikeout 😤 The Rays are just three outs away from the World Series! pic.twitter.com/47BpXTVDTe — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 20, 2026 Kelly’s escape came with Tampa Bay holding a 3-2 series advantage, needing one more victory to secure its third World Series appearance in franchise history. The Rays entered Monday’s matchup following a 3-1 victory in Game 5 on Sunday, when starter Drew Rasmussen limited Cleveland to one run over seven innings. That win gave the club back-to-back victories on the road and an opportunity to finish the best-of-seven series at home. The Guardians, meanwhile, faced elimination and needed to win Game 6 to force a decisive seventh contest. Kelly’s strikeout prevented Cleveland from capitalizing on one of its late scoring opportunities, maintaining the Rays’ two-run cushion heading into the bottom of the eighth. The play also continued Tampa Bay’s strong pitching throughout the postseason, helping the club secure its first World Series appearance since 2020. After escaping the eighth-inning jam, the Rays completed their 7-3 Game 6 victory over the Guardians, clinching the American League pennant and advancing to the 2026 World Series. item.title: Report: Chicago Bears Jonah Jackson week-to-week with a hip flexor
item.description: Oct 4, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears offensive line Jonah Jackson (73) against the New York Jets at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect According to a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , Chicago Bears starting right guard Jonah Jackson is dealing with a hip flexor and is considered week-to-week. Jackson left Sunday’s win against the Atlanta Falcons in the second half and was ruled doubtful to return. Second-year pro Luke Newman entered the game for Jackson and finished the game. Fowler added that Jackson’s availability for the Bears’ Thursday Night Game against the New England Patriots is “in doubt,” but the injury “shouldn’t be long-term.” Offensive coordinator Press Taylor met the media earlier today, and he discussed the possibility of replacing Jackson for Thursday’s game with either Newman or Jordan McFadden. “We’re excited about the depth we have,” Taylor said. Newman came in, did a good job to finish that game out for us. I think it’s worth noting McFadden started for us last year in the playoffs, and we were very comfortable with him starting at guard. And he did a good job in that game, so we’re excited about the depth of those guys. And we’ll see where Jonah’s at and if he’s got a chance to play on Thursday or not, but we are excited about some of the depth we have behind those guys as well on the inside.” The Bears did release an injury report today, allbeit it was just an estimation on how it would have been if they held more than a walk through, and Jackson was listed as a DNP with the hip and a quad injury. Also listed as did not practice were linebackers T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Jack Sanborn (consussion) and running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe). Linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad) and corner Tyrique Stevenson (hip) were listed on the injury report but as full participants. And that’s it. Quarterback Caleb Williams wasn’t listed at all.

item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

It had been a frustrating week, domestically and continentally, in two games on the road. On both occasions they had been caught cold, conceding the Bundesliga’s fastest goal at Augsburg and going 1-0 down in less than 90 seconds in Stavanger . Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, almost motionless in his seat as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. The sporting director, Max Eberl, who stood in for his coach in the post-match press conference, explained that the Belgian had been ill, not to mention Kompany’s current hip problem that had made the move from dressing room to pitchside slow and uncomfortable. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
